statement: The minimum number of real solutions over generic real input data is one.

source.location: Corollary IV, §4, author preprint printed page 31; proof pages 31–33
source.version: Author-hosted 37-page preprint, Corollary IV; journal publication identity separately verified

scope: The generic fibre for plane cubics of genus 1 through 9 points. For real-count assertions, all prescribed points and lines (including any specified contact point) are real and satisfy the genericity assumptions.

origin.inheritance_basis: A reduced generic complex fibre of cardinality one has trivial permutation action; for generic real inputs conjugation fixes its unique solution.

notes:
Elementary deduction from the recorded complex count one. Complex conjugation preserves the fibre for real input data, so its unique point is fixed and the solution curve is defined over R. A permutation action on a singleton is trivial. These deductions are supplied here explicitly; they are not attributed as separate theorems in the cited paper. The assertion concerns real solution curves, not reality of every point on a real curve.

Aluffi explicitly identifies these characteristic numbers as classical results of Maillard and Zeuthen. Those original claims and Aluffi’s rigorous verification are both cited; the modern proof is not presented as the first numerical claim. Any singleton real or monodromy assertion here is a deduction from the count.
